existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 removes the standalone `MedicinalProductInteraction` resource and folds interaction content into `ClinicalUseDefinition.type = "interaction"`. The main migration risks are resource identity/API breakage, mandatory and retyped `subject`, moved branch-specific fields with changed reference targets, and R6-only context that cannot be downgraded to R4. Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition changes but lower for official rationale because no local cross-version map was available.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Treat the migration as a structural transform: change resource identity, add the root discriminator, nest interaction details, update product/substance references, wrap CodeableConcept effects into CodeableReference, and preserve text/context fields through extensions or narrative when no base element exists.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same-name R6 resource is absent and that `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction` is the practical counterpart, based on the R6 StructureDefinition, package index, `fhir-old-types`, and interaction search parameter. Confidence would improve with official migration maps, narrative release notes, and terminology expansions.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
MedicinalProductInteraction has a resource-identity break: MedicinalProductInteraction resource is absent in R6 and interaction content is merged into ClinicalUseDefinition. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 95/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

6 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.

topFindings.title: MedicinalProductInteraction resource is absent in R6 and interaction content is merged into ClinicalUseDefinition
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: the resource name changes from `MedicinalProductInteraction` to `ClinicalUseDefinition`; raw R4 instances are also old-valid/new-invalid until transformed.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R4 free-text description has no direct R6 interaction field
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: copying the R4 `description` property into the R6 interaction branch is invalid; omitting it can create semantic data loss unless narrative or an extension is used.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 requires a root type discriminator and gates the interaction branch with invariants
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: a transformed instance that omits root `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` or confuses it with old `MedicinalProductInteraction.type` fails R6 validation.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Subject is now mandatory and represented as CodeableReference with changed targets
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with no subject fail the R6 minimum, and R4 references to removed target resource families require conversion before strict R6 validation.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Interactant item moved under the interaction branch and its reference targets changed
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: the old root path is not accepted in R6, and legacy references to `MedicinalProduct` or `Substance` are outside the R6 target list unless converted.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Interaction effect changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: generated models and FHIRPath expressions change from a CodeableConcept field to a CodeableReference wrapper; R6 reference-valued effects also create R6-to-R4 loss.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds interaction context fields absent from R4, including modifier status, route, severity, population, and library
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: optional R6 context, especially modifier `status`, has no direct R4 base representation; there is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break for this finding.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: Management actions are repeatable in R6, creating downgrade loss risk
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 can carry more than one management action, while R4 has only one slot; R4-to-R6 migration is a straightforward one-item array.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
